text:
Wyatt Kaiser is playing nearly 20 minutes a night on a Blackhawks blue line that's taking a beating, and he's been on the ice for a lot of it. The Athletic's Mark Lazerus noted that no player had been on for more five-on-five goals against this season. The Hawks get just 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) in his five-on-five minutes.

That's ugly, but not all of it is his. Chicago has also scored 11.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of luck that tends to swing back, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season had him playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league (bottom 1% by their impact), which drags a defenseman's raw numbers down. He isn't a point producer either way; six points in 20 games is about his level. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking does show a defenseman who joins the rush more than most (27% of his shots, against a typical 17%). The question for Chicago is whether he's a top-four defenseman being overexposed or just a third-pair player in a bigger job, and these minutes are the test.
